facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: The 2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports with their releases and the audited 2024 statements allow annual and quarterly series to be built, with the fourth quarter of 2025 derived by subtraction. Three points need care rather than repair. Reported Adjusted EBITDA includes tariff refund benefits that the full-year guidance excludes. facts.label: Analysis
facts.text: Gross debt at carrying value fell from USD 16,494 million at the end of FY2024 to USD 12,561 million at the end of FY2025 and stands at USD 12,580 million at September 26, 2026. The fall came from the IPO, whose net proceeds of USD 7,048 million funded a net repayment of borrowings of USD 4,092 million in FY2025 while free cash flow was USD 1,297 million, so deleveraging was a one-time change in the capital structure and not the result of cash generation. Reported EBITDA, which carries the distribution center fire losses, refinancing costs and other charges the issuer adds back, was USD 2,687 million for the twelve months to September 26, 2026 against USD 3,071 million in FY2025, so leverage on reported EBITDA rose from 4.09x to 4.68x while leverage on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA eased from 3.62x to 3.49x. rows.label: Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA for any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated from net income, interest, taxes and depreciation and amortization; it restricts comparison with the issuer's own measures; severity Low; the action that would close it is a stated reported EBITDA, which the issuer does not provide. - Short-term investments of USD 1,287 million at September 26, 2026 are counted as cash in net debt and liquidity but are a separate balance sheet line; net debt without them would be USD 10,259 million and net leverage on reported EBITDA 3.82x; severity Low; the action is to confirm the time deposits are freely accessible. - The 2031 notes of USD 1,250 million and the 2033 notes of USD 750 million, and other short-term debt of USD 1 million, are left out of the debt stack because no supplied document states their legal rank; this restricts cumulative leverage by rank, which is understated; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the 2026 indenture and the amendment to the credit agreement. - No statements for the borrower group, the guarantors or a restricted group are supplied, so leverage at the borrower level, and the effect of the holding company's tax receivable agreement and noncontrolling interests on cash reaching the borrower, cannot be measured; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the executed documents and any compliance reporting. - No carrying value by instrument is stated, so each instrument is shown at principal with one financing cost adjustment of USD -164 million; this restricts instrument-level leverage; severity Low; the action is the issuer's debt schedule, if one exists. - The issuer publishes no pro forma net debt for the prepayment of USD 750 million after quarter end, and the accrued interest paid with it is not stated, so pro forma net debt is shown as unchanged before that interest; severity Low; the action is the fourth quarter report. - The bed discontinuation cost is stated as USD 50 million to USD 200 million in the subsequent events note and USD 60 million to USD 210 million in the discussion, and the filing does not reconcile them; this restricts the size of excluded costs after the period; severity Low; the action is the fourth quarter report. - Reported nine-month 2026 EBITDA includes net tariff refund benefits of USD 324 million while the issuer's full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance excludes them, so the reported twelve month figure and the guidance are on different bases; severity Medium; the action is the issuer's guidance on a comparable basis. - FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,768 million comes from the registration statement, whose add-back lines differ from the 2025 annual report although the total add-backs agree; the FY2023 ratios on adjusted EBITDA are therefore on a slightly different definition; severity Low; no action needed beyond the label. - Lines printed in only some periods, such as the income taxes payable line before the IPO, the tax receivable agreement and deferred tax assets after it, short-term investments in 2026, and several financing lines, carry Not supplied cells rather than zero; the balance sheet also prints a dash for mezzanine equity after the IPO; severity Low; no action needed. - Segment assets are not reported, and the segment schedule covers net sales and Segment Adjusted EBITDA only; severity Low; no action is available. - Organic Sales growth is stated by the issuer only for Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 in the sources read, so earlier periods carry Not supplied cells in the dashboard; severity Low; no action needed. - The 2025 annual report omits management's report on internal control for a newly public company, which limits assurance over the statements beyond the audit opinion; severity Low; the action is the next annual report.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Medline's business supports creditors, but owner claims on group cash are the main risk: sponsors and the Mills family held about 67.0% of the votes in February 2026, and a USD 4,415 million tax receivable agreement is payable from group cash. IPO equity repaid the euro term loans and most of the 2028 dollar term loans in December 2025, although USD 1,970 million of the proceeds went to pre-IPO owners. Sponsor affiliates and an early investor sold a further USD 6.2 billion of shares in 2026, and the company received none of it. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the view that owner claims are the main risk is that creditors are being repaid and the owners are leaving without taking company cash. Total debt fell by USD 3,933 million in FY2025, sponsor-affiliated holdings of the company's debt are down to USD 41 million, no dividend is planned, the 2026 sell-downs were paid for by public investors, the audit committee at the offering had no owner designee, and at the September 25, 2026 price the equity is worth about USD 45.6 billion against total debt of USD 12,580 million, so a very large equity cushion sits beneath the debt. The view would soften if the executed debt documents show tight limits on distributions, or if a proxy statement shows an independent board majority, and it would harden if payments under the tax receivable agreement begin to exceed the cash tax savings, if repurchases are used to buy Medline Holdings units from the owners, or if a new owner distribution is paid while operating costs from the fire, recall and warning letters are still being incurred. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The IPO of December 18, 2025 priced Class A stock at USD 29.00 and raised net proceeds of USD 7,048 million after USD 157 million of underwriting discounts, before offering expenses of about USD 40 million. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt in 2026 was a single refinancing on May 28 and one voluntary prepayment. Medline Borrower, LP and Medline Co-Issuer, Inc. issued USD 1,250 million of senior secured notes due June 15, 2031 and USD 750 million of senior secured notes due June 15, 2033, and Medline Borrower, LP replaced the 2030 dollar term loan with a USD 2,750 million loan due 2033 at SOFR plus 1.50%; the uses were repayment of USD 762 million of 2028 term loan, USD 724 million of the 2030 term loan and redemption of USD 500 million of secured notes due 2029, with fees. On October 22, 2026 the company prepaid USD 750 million of the new term loan from cash, which leaves USD 1,993 million before any further amortisation, and expects a loss on extinguishment of about USD 21 million in the fourth quarter. The rank, lien and guarantors of the 2031 and 2033 notes are not established, because the 2026 indenture is not supplied. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the issuer reaffirmed Adjusted EBITDA guidance, raised organic sales guidance to 10.0% to 10.5% from 9.0% to 10.0%, grew third-quarter net sales 10.41% and Adjusted EBITDA 11.76%, although the latter includes USD 81 million of refunds, and holds equity worth about USD 45.6 billion at the September 25, 2026 price against total debt of USD 12,580 million, so a very large cushion sits under creditors and a weak quarter would not threaten debt service before 2029. The issuer attributes the pressure on margin to inventory cost inflation, higher operating expenses and customer mix, some of which could fade, but the filings do not show that it will. The view would improve if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA reaches the top of the implied range, the warning letters close without restrictions, and the 2029 notes are refinanced early; it would worsen if the fourth quarter falls below USD 828 million, if more than 35% of the revolver is drawn, if repurchases begin while remediation costs run, or if a large Prime Vendor or purchasing group relationship is lost. facts.label: Business model and operating drivers
facts.text: Medline manufactures about one-third of its own-brand medical-surgical products and distributes the rest of that brand and third-party products through a network of 70 sites and an owned truck fleet, serving hospitals, post-acute and physician offices under multi-year Prime Vendor agreements. The credit mechanism is that distribution volume and contract tenure give revenue visibility, while the own-brand mix earns the margin: Medline Brand's margin was 26.1% in nine months 2026 against 4.7% for Supply Chain Solutions, so the shift of growth towards Prime Vendor distribution raises revenue faster than earnings. Cost flexibility is moderate: capital expenditure is low at 1.57% of net sales, but inflation in inventory cost, customer mix and operating expense took the gross margin to 26.13% in nine months 2026 from 27.14% in nine months 2025 even with tariff refunds in cost of goods sold. facts.label: Market frameworks
facts.text: Competition is a creditor concern because it sets pricing: the issuer competes with large distributors for Prime Vendor agreements and faces buying groups that can push prices down, so a lost agreement removes volume and margin together, as the USD 227 million of FY2025 sales lost to departing Prime Vendor customers shows. Supplier power is limited, with no sourcing partner above 5% of spend, but 5% of cost of goods sold comes from China, which ties the cost base to tariffs. The political and regulatory factors that matter for credit are tariffs and their refunds, FDA enforcement and health policy affecting hospital spending; the first adds volatility to margin, the second can limit products and the third can limit pricing, and none of them is quantified beyond the amounts the issuer reports. facts.text: The financial profile is stronger than at the end of FY2024 but the trend is flattered by one-offs. Scale is large and cost and capex flexibility adequate; margin stability is weak because the 2026 gain rests on refunds; free cash flow stability is moderate for the same reason; liquidity is strong at USD 4,570 million; the ability to refinance is adequate but concentrated in 2029; financial policy and governance are adequate with owner claims on cash as the weak point. Total debt fell to USD 12,580 million from USD 16,494 million at the end of FY2024, and leverage on reported EBITDA was 4.09x at the end of FY2025 and 4.68x at September 26, 2026, down from 5.34x at the end of FY2024, the rise since FY2025 reflecting fire and other charges that lowered reported EBITDA; adjusted leverage fell to 3.49x from 4.91x. facts.text: Over the next one to two years the tailwinds are organic sales growth guided at 10.0% to 10.5% for FY2026, a lower interest bill, the expected recovery of the remaining insured fire loss, and USD 80 million to USD 90 million of annual savings targeted from the October 2026 restructuring. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most credible downside starts with product quality, not demand. An FDA action following the three unresolved warning letters, at the Northfield, Glens Falls and Waukegan sites, could restrict shipments of affected Medline Brand products; because that segment earned 82.84% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, group earnings would fall faster than sales, the tariff refunds, of which USD 399 million of an expected USD 507 million has been received, would not support later periods, and the excluded costs of the bed exit and restructuring would still be paid in cash. Liquidity of USD 4,570 million and USD 69 million of scheduled principal before 2029 mean the group would not face a liquidity shortfall in this case; the pressure would come as leverage stays near the 3.84x refund-free adjusted level or higher into 2028, when the USD 8,027 million due in 2029 would be refinanced and the revolver's maturity springs. Management levers are the unused repurchase authorisation, which need not be used, and the capital expenditure plan of up to USD 600 million for FY2026, which is mainly growth spending on automation, new distribution centers and kitting capacity and could be slowed, although the sources do not say how much is committed. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Medline presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a contract base and a profitable own-brand segment, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that include one-off refunds, product-quality enforcement risk and a concentrated 2029 maturity wall. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive and capital needs are low, though 2026 is flattered, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the fourth-quarter result, the closing of the warning letters and market conditions in 2028. The primary downside path is an FDA action on own-brand products while refunds end. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, a rating or market price, and a forecast. Top risk: earnings quality. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-06

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings and releases support the requested credit snapshot of Medline Inc. through the quarter ended September 26, 2026, with limits: no executed debt documents, ratings or market quotes, so covenant, structural and pricing views would rest on the issuer's own summaries.

The 2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports with their releases and the audited 2024 statements allow annual and quarterly series to be built, with the fourth quarter of 2025 derived by subtraction. Three points need care rather than repair. Reported Adjusted EBITDA includes tariff refund benefits that the full-year guidance excludes. The release's net leverage uses principal debt, not the balance-sheet carrying value. The term loan prepayment of USD 750 million after quarter end is not reflected in published net debt. Nothing later than November 4, 2026 is covered.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage on carrying-value debt is 4.68x reported EBITDA for the twelve months to September 26, 2026, against 3.49x on the issuer's adjusted measure, so creditor risk turns on how much of USD 914 million of add-backs is real.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 62; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

Debt fell from USD 16,494 million at the end of FY2024 to USD 12,561 million at the end of FY2025 and is USD 12,580 million at September 26, 2026, so the gain came from IPO equity proceeds, not cash generation. Interest paid over twelve months is USD 700 million, covered 3.84x by reported EBITDA. Cash of USD 3,608 million, including short-term investments, and an undrawn revolver of USD 962 million sit against scheduled principal of only USD 69 million before 2029, when USD 8,027 million falls due. A USD 750 million prepayment after quarter end leaves net debt unchanged before accrued interest.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-11
### Analysis

Gross debt at carrying value fell from USD 16,494 million at the end of FY2024 to USD 12,561 million at the end of FY2025 and stands at USD 12,580 million at September 26, 2026. The fall came from the IPO, whose net proceeds of USD 7,048 million funded a net repayment of borrowings of USD 4,092 million in FY2025 while free cash flow was USD 1,297 million, so deleveraging was a one-time change in the capital structure and not the result of cash generation. Reported EBITDA, which carries the distribution center fire losses, refinancing costs and other charges the issuer adds back, was USD 2,687 million for the twelve months to September 26, 2026 against USD 3,071 million in FY2025, so leverage on reported EBITDA rose from 4.09x to 4.68x while leverage on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA eased from 3.62x to 3.49x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12

The gap between the two measures is USD 914 million of add-backs over the twelve months, 25.38% of adjusted EBITDA, of which other non-core charges are USD 476 million and the non-cash inventory adjustment for last-in, first-out reserves is USD 199 million. The mechanism for creditors is that market and covenant style leverage uses the adjusted figure, while cash must still pay for the fire, recall, remediation and refinancing costs that the add-backs remove: the issuer excludes estimated costs of the bed discontinuation of USD 50 million to USD 200 million (USD 60 million to USD 210 million in the discussion) from adjusted EBITDA yet expects to incur them in the fourth quarter of 2026 and 2027. Reported figures for nine months 2026 also include net tariff refund benefits of USD 324 million that the full-year guidance excludes.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation CALC-04

Cash interest paid fell to USD 700 million over twelve months from USD 944 million in FY2025, lifting cover on reported EBITDA to 3.84x from 3.25x, because the IPO repayment and the second-quarter refinancing lowered the cost of debt: variable-rate debt averages 6.07% against 7.10% at the end of FY2025. Operating cash flow of USD 2,152 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,515 million a year earlier is flattered by a USD 606 million swing in working capital, an inflow of USD 105 million, which includes USD 446 million from accrued expenses, against an outflow of USD 501 million, and by tariff refunds received of about USD 399 million, part of which is owed to customers. Free cash flow of USD 1,804 million for nine months should therefore be read as above a sustainable level.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-10

Liquidity is USD 4,570 million, made up of cash and short-term investments of USD 3,608 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 962 million, against scheduled principal of USD 69 million across the rest of 2026, 2027 and 2028, so there is no refinancing pressure before 2029. In 2029 USD 8,027 million, 62.99% of principal, falls due across the secured and unsecured notes, and the revolver, which matures in 2029, carries a springing maturity 91 days before the maturity of the notes and term loans. The springing first-lien net leverage covenant of 8.3x applies only if more than 35% of the revolver is drawn and was not tested because nothing is drawn.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-08

After quarter end the issuer prepaid USD 750 million of the term loan from cash on hand on 2026-10-22, which lowers gross debt and cash equally, so net debt stays at USD 8,972 million and net leverage on reported EBITDA stays at 3.34x before accrued interest, which the filing does not state; interest expense should fall in later periods and a loss on extinguishment of about USD 21 million is expected in the fourth quarter. The repurchase authorisation of up to USD 1 billion, with nothing yet repurchased, is the main use of cash that could reverse part of the net debt reduction.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation CALC-11

Outside Total Debt the balance sheet carries a tax receivable agreement liability of USD 4,403 million (USD 4,415 million in the note, which includes USD 12 million due within a year), noncontrolling interests of USD 7,585 million, and, at the end of FY2025, operating lease liabilities of USD 452 million inside accrued and other liabilities. The tax receivable agreement is an obligation of Medline Inc. rather than the borrower, but it is funded by distributions from Medline Holdings, so it can draw on the same group cash that services debt. Customer rebate accruals of USD 406 million at the end of FY2025 and trade payables of USD 1,209 million at September 26, 2026 are non-debt float that helped fund working capital. Other claims are small against debt: unconditional purchase obligations of USD 710 million over five years and beyond, a pension projected benefit obligation of USD 61 million at the end of FY2025, and an ethylene oxide settlement liability of USD 174 million at the end of FY2024 that was paid in cash of USD 166 million during FY2025, leaving none outstanding.

The strongest contrary evidence is that adjusted leverage of 3.49x and net leverage of 2.49x on adjusted EBITDA are well below the 8.3x springing covenant level, although that covenant uses its own EBITDA definition, with liquidity of USD 4,570 million and no maturity before 2029; reported EBITDA is also depressed by fire losses that were net of USD 100 million of insurance recovered and by USD 46 million of refinancing costs, so recovery of the remaining insured loss would move reported leverage towards the adjusted figure. What would worsen the view is growth in the costs the issuer excludes, such as the bed discontinuation of up to USD 210 million and restructuring of USD 20 million to USD 30 million, or a revolver draw above 35% that would bring the covenant into test.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 69; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

The issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA here is calculated as net income plus interest, taxes and depreciation and amortisation. The release's Net Leverage of 2.5x uses principal debt of USD 12,743 million, deducts cash and short-term investments of USD 3,608 million and divides by adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,601 million, whereas this module uses carrying value of USD 12,580 million, a difference of USD 163 million, and obtains 2.49x on the same adjusted measure.

## Gaps

- The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA for any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated from net income, interest, taxes and depreciation and amortization; it restricts comparison with the issuer's own measures; severity Low; the action that would close it is a stated reported EBITDA, which the issuer does not provide.

- Short-term investments of USD 1,287 million at September 26, 2026 are counted as cash in net debt and liquidity but are a separate balance sheet line; net debt without them would be USD 10,259 million and net leverage on reported EBITDA 3.82x; severity Low; the action is to confirm the time deposits are freely accessible.

- The 2031 notes of USD 1,250 million and the 2033 notes of USD 750 million, and other short-term debt of USD 1 million, are left out of the debt stack because no supplied document states their legal rank; this restricts cumulative leverage by rank, which is understated; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the 2026 indenture and the amendment to the credit agreement.

- No statements for the borrower group, the guarantors or a restricted group are supplied, so leverage at the borrower level, and the effect of the holding company's tax receivable agreement and noncontrolling interests on cash reaching the borrower, cannot be measured; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the executed documents and any compliance reporting.

- No carrying value by instrument is stated, so each instrument is shown at principal with one financing cost adjustment of USD -164 million; this restricts instrument-level leverage; severity Low; the action is the issuer's debt schedule, if one exists.

- The issuer publishes no pro forma net debt for the prepayment of USD 750 million after quarter end, and the accrued interest paid with it is not stated, so pro forma net debt is shown as unchanged before that interest; severity Low; the action is the fourth quarter report.

- The bed discontinuation cost is stated as USD 50 million to USD 200 million in the subsequent events note and USD 60 million to USD 210 million in the discussion, and the filing does not reconcile them; this restricts the size of excluded costs after the period; severity Low; the action is the fourth quarter report.

- Reported nine-month 2026 EBITDA includes net tariff refund benefits of USD 324 million while the issuer's full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance excludes them, so the reported twelve month figure and the guidance are on different bases; severity Medium; the action is the issuer's guidance on a comparable basis.

- FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,768 million comes from the registration statement, whose add-back lines differ from the 2025 annual report although the total add-backs agree; the FY2023 ratios on adjusted EBITDA are therefore on a slightly different definition; severity Low; no action needed beyond the label.

- Lines printed in only some periods, such as the income taxes payable line before the IPO, the tax receivable agreement and deferred tax assets after it, short-term investments in 2026, and several financing lines, carry Not supplied cells rather than zero; the balance sheet also prints a dash for mezzanine equity after the IPO; severity Low; no action needed.
- Segment assets are not reported, and the segment schedule covers net sales and Segment Adjusted EBITDA only; severity Low; no action is available.
- Organic Sales growth is stated by the issuer only for Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 in the sources read, so earlier periods carry Not supplied cells in the dashboard; severity Low; no action needed.

- The 2025 annual report omits management's report on internal control for a newly public company, which limits assurance over the statements beyond the audit opinion; severity Low; the action is the next annual report.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Medline's business supports creditors, but owner claims on group cash are the main risk: sponsors and the Mills family held about 67.0% of the votes in February 2026, and a USD 4,415 million tax receivable agreement is payable from group cash. IPO equity repaid the euro term loans and most of the 2028 dollar term loans in December 2025, although USD 1,970 million of the proceeds went to pre-IPO owners. Sponsor affiliates and an early investor sold a further USD 6.2 billion of shares in 2026, and the company received none of it.

### Key findings

The business earns its profit in the brand segment and grows its volume in a thin-margin distribution segment, so creditors depend on Medline Brand. Medline Brand gave 82.84% of segment Adjusted EBITDA on 46.49% of net sales in nine months 2026, while Supply Chain Solutions grew its sales 15.1% and saw its margin fall to 4.7% from 5.5%, which the issuer links to lower-margin Prime Vendor customers. Management says its own brand earns higher margins as customers convert to it; the filings give the average Prime Vendor mix of 35% Medline Brand, which sizes the room left to convert, but not how fast conversion has proceeded.

The brand margin gain comes from tariff relief, not underlying improvement. Guidance for FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3.3 billion to USD 3.4 billion also excludes the refunds.

Revenue is sticky but concentrated, so a single lost relationship matters more than the average retention suggests. Prime Vendor agreements, usually five-year terms, gave 63.4% of FY2025 net sales and sales to members of three purchasing groups gave 69%, while the five largest US customers gave 11.3%. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the view that owner claims are the main risk is that creditors are being repaid and the owners are leaving without taking company cash. Total debt fell by USD 3,933 million in FY2025, sponsor-affiliated holdings of the company's debt are down to USD 41 million, no dividend is planned, the 2026 sell-downs were paid for by public investors, the audit committee at the offering had no owner designee, and at the September 25, 2026 price the equity is worth about USD 45.6 billion against total debt of USD 12,580 million, so a very large equity cushion sits beneath the debt. The view would soften if the executed debt documents show tight limits on distributions, or if a proxy statement shows an independent board majority, and it would harden if payments under the tax receivable agreement begin to exceed the cash tax savings, if repurchases are used to buy Medline Holdings units from the owners, or if a new owner distribution is paid while operating costs from the fire, recall and warning letters are still being incurred.

### Limitations

- The executed credit agreement, indentures and security documents are not supplied, so the room for distributions and the guarantee structure rest on filing summaries; if payment baskets prove wide the owner risk level would move up, if tight it would move down.

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the current board, committees, owner stakes and pay are taken from the November 2025 registration statement and February 2026 voting figures; the control conclusion could be out of date after the two sell-downs.
- Fund vintage, entry price, equity invested and exit plans of the sponsors are not stated, so sponsor willingness to support creditors is not assessed and none is assumed.

- Owner ownership percentages are blank in the registration statement tables, so the split of the 67.0% between the sponsors and the Mills family is not established and sponsor concentration cannot be refined.
- Supply Chain Solutions has no product split and no segment assets are reported, so conclusions on distribution margins rest on segment totals.
- The share of Prime Vendor sales under agreements that can be ended for convenience is not stated, so contract durability is described but not measured.

# Fundamental credit for Medline Inc. as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit for Medline Inc. (issuer mdln-2046386), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business risk, financial profile, refinancing capacity, owner behaviour and downside path, built from the eight supplied filings and releases and the three earlier analyses. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Medline's credit profile is adequate: liquidity of USD 4,570 million and no material maturity before 2029 give creditors time, but weak earnings quality, product-quality enforcement risk and USD 8,027 million due in 2029 make the next two years of results decisive.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

Leverage is 4.68x on reported EBITDA and 3.49x on the issuer's adjusted figure for the twelve months to September 26, 2026, and it is 3.84x on adjusted EBITDA once USD 324 million of one-off tariff refunds is removed. Net debt is USD 8,972 million at September 26, 2026, and is unchanged at USD 8,972 million pro forma for the USD 750 million prepayment on October 22, 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02
### Key findings

Earnings quality is the weakest part of the credit, because a quarter of adjusted EBITDA is add-backs and part of the 2026 gain is one-off. Add-backs were USD 914 million, 25.38% of adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months, and nine-month Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 324 million of net tariff refunds that the issuer's FY2026 guidance excludes; without them the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin is 10.76% against 12.89% a year earlier. Guidance of USD 3.3 billion to USD 3.4 billion implies fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 828 million to USD 928 million against USD 805 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, so the guided year needs underlying earnings to grow 2.86% to 15.28% in that quarter. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA growth of 11.76% falls to 2.33% without the USD 81 million of refunds recognised in that quarter.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-12

Liquidity is the main support, because scheduled debt can be paid for years without the capital markets. Liquidity is USD 4,570 million, made of cash and short-term investments of USD 3,608 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 962 million after USD 38 million of letters of credit, against only USD 69 million of scheduled principal before 2029; the cash figure is before the USD 750 million prepayment of October 22, 2026, and pro forma cash is not established. The only financial covenant, a first lien net leverage limit of 8.3x, applies to the revolver only when more than 35% of it is drawn, which is USD 350 million, so it has not been tested, and headroom is not calculable because the credit agreement's EBITDA definition is not supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation CALC-05

Refinancing is the main constraint, because USD 8,027 million, 62.99% of principal, falls due in 2029 and the revolver's maturity springs to about the end of 2028. The 2029 amount is secured notes of USD 5,500 million, unsecured notes of USD 2,500 million and USD 27 million of term loan amortisation, and the revolver, which matures in July 2029, falls due 91 days before the earliest note maturity on April 1, 2029. Market access is shown by the IPO and by USD 2,000 million of new notes in May 2026, and liquidity covers 56.93% of the 2029 amount, but no rating or market price is supplied, so the cost of refinancing is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

The business is large, contract-based and cash generative, but cash conversion is moderate and was flattered in 2026. Net sales were USD 28,432 million in FY2025, Prime Vendor agreements gave 63.4% of them and purchasing groups 69%, and capital expenditure was only 1.57% of net sales. Free cash flow was USD 1,297 million in FY2025, 37.41% of adjusted EBITDA; the USD 1,804 million for nine months 2026 is 64.52% but includes about USD 399 million of tariff refunds received, and without them it is USD 1,405 million, 56.84% of adjusted EBITDA without the refunds.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 49; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-08

Quality and site risks are real cash costs that the issuer excludes from Adjusted EBITDA. The Tracy distribution center fire left USD 316 million of net losses after USD 100 million of insurance recoveries, three FDA warning letters are unresolved, the Medline Brand bed exit is expected to cost USD 60 million to USD 210 million and a restructuring USD 20 million to USD 30 million, together USD 80 million to USD 240 million, or 2.98% to 8.93% of reported twelve-month EBITDA. The amounts are manageable against liquidity, but an FDA action that limited distribution of affected brand products would reach the segment that earned 82.84% of segment Adjusted EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-09

Owner behaviour is mixed and the sponsor and governance risk level is medium. A tax receivable agreement liability of USD 4,415 million, 35.10% of total debt, is payable by Medline Inc. from group distributions, owners sold USD 6.2 billion of shares in 2026 with no proceeds to the company, and the board authorised repurchases of up to USD 1 billion; against that, IPO equity repaid USD 4,011 million of term loan principal, no priming or creditor-adverse amendment is described, and the executed debt documents that would limit owner payouts are not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation CALC-10

Interest burden is falling and rate exposure is small. Cash interest paid was USD 700 million over twelve months against USD 944 million in FY2025, the weighted average effective rate on debt is 5.24% against 5.72% at the end of FY2025, and variable-rate debt of USD 2,743 million is 21.53% of principal, before the prepayment; reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.84x and adjusted EBITDA 5.14x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the issuer reaffirmed Adjusted EBITDA guidance, raised organic sales guidance to 10.0% to 10.5% from 9.0% to 10.0%, grew third-quarter net sales 10.41% and Adjusted EBITDA 11.76%, although the latter includes USD 81 million of refunds, and holds equity worth about USD 45.6 billion at the September 25, 2026 price against total debt of USD 12,580 million, so a very large cushion sits under creditors and a weak quarter would not threaten debt service before 2029. The issuer attributes the pressure on margin to inventory cost inflation, higher operating expenses and customer mix, some of which could fade, but the filings do not show that it will. The view would improve if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA reaches the top of the implied range, the warning letters close without restrictions, and the 2029 notes are refinanced early; it would worsen if the fourth quarter falls below USD 828 million, if more than 35% of the revolver is drawn, if repurchases begin while remediation costs run, or if a large Prime Vendor or purchasing group relationship is lost.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 69; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-12
### Limitations

- No credit rating, agency view or market price for the debt is supplied, so the conclusion on refinancing cost rests on the issuer's own issuance record and cannot be tested against what the market would charge for the 2029 amount.

- The adjusted figures use the issuer's own add-back definitions and the refund-free figures in this answer are calculated on the assumption that the net refund benefit sits fully inside Adjusted EBITDA, as the issuer states for nine months; if later refunds or customer repayments change, the earnings-quality conclusion moves with them.

- Covenant headroom is not calculable because the credit agreement's definition of consolidated EBITDA is not supplied, so the statement that the covenant is not tested rests on the issuer's own disclosure and on undrawn revolver borrowings.
- Guidance covers FY2026 only and no forecast is built here, so the view that the 2029 amount can be refinanced assumes earnings stay near the twelve-month level and is not a projection.
- Pro forma cash after the October 22, 2026 prepayment is not stated by the earlier financial analysis, so liquidity after that date is described only as lower by the amount prepaid.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is a large contract base that gives visibility. Prime Vendor agreements gave 63.4% of FY2025 net sales on typical five-year terms with average retention above 98% over five years, which supports predictable volumes and lets the issuer plan capacity with about 25% spare capacity, although both statements are the issuer's own.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second strength is a profitable own-brand segment. Medline Brand earned 82.84% of segment Adjusted EBITDA on 46.49% of net sales in nine months 2026, so debt service depends on a segment with a 26.1% margin, and the manufacturing of about one-third of own-brand products gives some control over cost and quality.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation CALC-11

The third strength is liquidity with no near-term maturities. Liquidity of USD 4,570 million covers scheduled principal before 2029 of USD 69 million 66.23 times, and the only maintenance covenant applies only if more than 35% of the revolver is drawn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation CALC-05

The fourth strength is deleveraging and lower interest cost. IPO equity cut total debt by USD 3,933 million in FY2025, and the IPO repayment and the May 2026 refinancing cut the weighted average effective rate to 5.24% from 5.72%, which lifted reported EBITDA cover of cash interest to 3.84x from 3.25x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 159; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-14

The first weakness is earnings quality. A quarter of adjusted EBITDA is add-backs and USD 324 million of one-off tariff refunds sits inside nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, so leverage on a refund-free basis is 3.84x and not 3.49x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-04

The second weakness is product-quality and site risk. Three FDA warning letters, the bed exit and the fire loss are cash costs outside Adjusted EBITDA, and an FDA restriction on distribution would hit the segment that provides most of the segment earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-11

The third weakness is customer concentration and distribution margin dilution. Purchasing groups gave 69% of net sales, the five largest customers 11.3%, and the Supply Chain Solutions margin fell to 4.7% from 5.5% as lower-margin Prime Vendor customers grew, so growth adds revenue faster than earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 61; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-11

The fourth weakness is concentration of maturities in 2029. USD 8,027 million falls due in one year, the revolver's maturity springs inside it, and the rank, lien and guarantors of the 2031 and 2033 notes are not established, so the structure of the later debt cannot be tested.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-06

The fifth weakness is owner claims on cash. The tax receivable agreement liability of USD 4,415 million is 35.10% of total debt, is payable from group distributions, and grows as owners exchange units, while a repurchase authorisation of up to USD 1 billion is unused.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 45; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-10
### Business model and operating drivers

Medline manufactures about one-third of its own-brand medical-surgical products and distributes the rest of that brand and third-party products through a network of 70 sites and an owned truck fleet, serving hospitals, post-acute and physician offices under multi-year Prime Vendor agreements. The credit mechanism is that distribution volume and contract tenure give revenue visibility, while the own-brand mix earns the margin: Medline Brand's margin was 26.1% in nine months 2026 against 4.7% for Supply Chain Solutions, so the shift of growth towards Prime Vendor distribution raises revenue faster than earnings. Cost flexibility is moderate: capital expenditure is low at 1.57% of net sales, but inflation in inventory cost, customer mix and operating expense took the gross margin to 26.13% in nine months 2026 from 27.14% in nine months 2025 even with tariff refunds in cost of goods sold.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mdln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11–15; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-13
### Market frameworks

Competition is a creditor concern because it sets pricing: the issuer competes with large distributors for Prime Vendor agreements and faces buying groups that can push prices down, so a lost agreement removes volume and margin together, as the USD 227 million of FY2025 sales lost to departing Prime Vendor customers shows. Supplier power is limited, with no sourcing partner above 5% of spend, but 5% of cost of goods sold comes from China, which ties the cost base to tariffs. The political and regulatory factors that matter for credit are tariffs and their refunds, FDA enforcement and health policy affecting hospital spending; the first adds volatility to margin, the second can limit products and the third can limit pricing, and none of them is quantified beyond the amounts the issuer reports.
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is stronger than at the end of FY2024 but the trend is flattered by one-offs. Scale is large and cost and capex flexibility adequate; margin stability is weak because the 2026 gain rests on refunds; free cash flow stability is moderate for the same reason; liquidity is strong at USD 4,570 million; the ability to refinance is adequate but concentrated in 2029; financial policy and governance are adequate with owner claims on cash as the weak point. Total debt fell to USD 12,580 million from USD 16,494 million at the end of FY2024, and leverage on reported EBITDA was 4.09x at the end of FY2025 and 4.68x at September 26, 2026, down from 5.34x at the end of FY2024, the rise since FY2025 reflecting fire and other charges that lowered reported EBITDA; adjusted leverage fell to 3.49x from 4.91x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next one to two years the tailwinds are organic sales growth guided at 10.0% to 10.5% for FY2026, a lower interest bill, the expected recovery of the remaining insured fire loss, and USD 80 million to USD 90 million of annual savings targeted from the October 2026 restructuring. The headwinds are the excluded costs of bed exit and restructuring in the fourth quarter of 2026 and in 2027, tariff costs of about USD 277 million in nine months 2026 before refunds, FDA remediation costs, and customer mix. Over three to five years the 2029 maturities, the unit exchanges that raise the tax receivable agreement liability, and the repurchase authorisation decide whether deleveraging continues; the issuer states no medium-term target, so none is assumed.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex9913q26pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-03
### Downside scenario

The most credible downside starts with product quality, not demand. An FDA action following the three unresolved warning letters, at the Northfield, Glens Falls and Waukegan sites, could restrict shipments of affected Medline Brand products; because that segment earned 82.84% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, group earnings would fall faster than sales, the tariff refunds, of which USD 399 million of an expected USD 507 million has been received, would not support later periods, and the excluded costs of the bed exit and restructuring would still be paid in cash. Liquidity of USD 4,570 million and USD 69 million of scheduled principal before 2029 mean the group would not face a liquidity shortfall in this case; the pressure would come as leverage stays near the 3.84x refund-free adjusted level or higher into 2028, when the USD 8,027 million due in 2029 would be refinanced and the revolver's maturity springs. Management levers are the unused repurchase authorisation, which need not be used, and the capital expenditure plan of up to USD 600 million for FY2026, which is mainly growth spending on automation, new distribution centers and kitting capacity and could be slowed, although the sources do not say how much is committed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 50–51; 10-Q_2026-09-26_mdln-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-05
### Overall credit view

Overall, Medline presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a contract base and a profitable own-brand segment, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that include one-off refunds, product-quality enforcement risk and a concentrated 2029 maturity wall. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive and capital needs are low, though 2026 is flattered, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the fourth-quarter result, the closing of the warning letters and market conditions in 2028. The primary downside path is an FDA action on own-brand products while refunds end. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, a rating or market price, and a forecast. Top risk: earnings quality.
